title: Fold canonical duplicate-claim validation into the entry pass
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView.__post_init__() already walks every retained SparseTensorEntry to validate exact axis bindings, label membership and canonical _entry_order. For already-canonical input, it then performed a second full traversal over ordered_entries solely to reject repeated coordinate/relation claims, even though adjacent canonical _entry_order values already expose the same semantic-key duplication during the first validation pass. At the declared one-million-entry ceiling this is a redundant O(entries) container walk on the canonical construction path.
primary_claim: TensorView construction now rejects adjacent duplicate coordinate/relation claims while it is already validating canonical entry order, reusing the previously computed _entry_order tuple. Canonical entry tuples therefore do not require the former second duplicate-validation traversal. If input is non-canonical, the existing deterministic sort fallback still performs a post-sort duplicate scan so non-adjacent duplicate claims remain fail-closed.
gardener_decision: Reuse the canonical order tuple already computed for each entry instead of introducing a duplicate-key set, cache, semantic-key index, alternate Tensor representation or separate validation service. Keep the post-sort duplicate scan only on the non-canonical fallback path where duplicate claims may have been non-adjacent before sorting.
acceptance: canonical TensorView entry validation retains exact axis-binding and declared-label checks
canonical entry tuples are reused and do not require a second full duplicate-claim traversal
duplicate coordinate/relation claims remain fail-closed even when value or evidence differs
non-canonical input retains deterministic sorting followed by duplicate-claim rejection

The focused _CoordinateReadBoundEntry regression gives each canonical entry a budget of two coordinates reads: one for binding validation and one for _entry_order construction. It therefore fails on the former second duplicate-validation traversal while the new canonical path completes and reuses the same immutable entries tuple. A companion regression preserves fail-closed rejection for duplicate coordinate/relation claims with different scalar/evidence payloads.
